usage: This is the standard, universal way to say thank you in Modern Standard Arabic. It is used in all contexts, from formal writing and news broadcasts to everyday speech. To be more specific or formal, pronouns are attached to the preposition li to specify who is being thanked.

variants.label: to a man
variants.note: Used when directly addressing a single male.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Used when directly addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing multiple people or a mixed-gender group.

variants.label: very much
variants.note: Used to express deeper gratitude or in more formal contexts.

responses.english: Don't mention it (literally: no thanks for a duty)
You are very welcome (literally: with spaciousness and ease)

examples.english: Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you all for your attendance today.

examples.arabic: أَقولُ لَكَ شُكْراً مِنْ أَعْماقِ قَلْبي.
examples.transliteration: aqoolu laka shukran min a3maqi qalbee.
examples.english: I say thank you to you from the bottom of my heart.
